item.title: Cloud-Init ISOs in Pure Go with go-proxmox
item.description: Proxmox’s built-in cloud-init support is fine for the basics: a user, an SSH key, an IP config. It falls apart the second you want your own user-data, vendor-data or a real network-config, because the GUI and the ci* options only expose a handful of fields, and the escape hatch (cicustom pointing at snippet files) means getting files onto the Proxmox host’s filesystem first. The usual alternative is building a nocloud ISO yourself with genisoimage or mkisofs, which means a system dependency on whatever machine runs your automation, a different package name on every OS, and a subprocess to babysit.

item.title: go-diskfs: Getting Rock Ridge Working for Joliet on Windows
item.description:
go-proxmox has had a CloudInit() helper since 2023. It builds a small nocloud ISO in Go, uploads it to Proxmox and mounts it on the VM as a CD-ROM. It’s always worked fine for Linux guests. It has never worked for Windows guests running cloudbase-init, and the reason is a filesystem extension from 1995 called Joliet.

Getting it fixed took three PRs to go-diskfs over about seven weeks, plus a bug report from a user who actually ran it on Windows, which turned out to be the most important part.
